claims.text: Czech parliamentary account; restricted electorate Separate institutions

The Czech parliamentary account distinguishes Prague’s Bohemian Diet from Vienna’s Imperial Council under a shared emperor. Bounded land responsibilities and restricted electoral representation remain explicit. Shared dynastic authority did not erase separate institutions or establish equal participation; the 1918 republic is outside this comparison.
Did the shared ruler eliminate the separate Bohemian Diet? Prague’s separate Land Diet and Vienna’s Imperial Council coexisted

claims.text: What evidence defeats “one ruler means one uniform assembly”? A separate Bohemian Diet met in Prague while the Imperial Council was in Vienna; the account identifies bounded land responsibilities.

The bounded 1861/1867 institutions are not modern sovereign city polities. Shared emperor does not establish uniform administration or universal Czech/German/Slovak representation; restricted electoral participation stays visible.
